scope: Stage 0 no-GPU design audit; placement is planned, not emitted

current_hook.trigger: griddepcontrol.launch_dependents appended at body end by default, or prepended for start

target_placement_rule: after index/pointer/accumulator setup and immediately before the first access to the buffer owned by the split edge; for a consumer with several RAW producers this rule only becomes single-wait-safe after the multi-producer capability is proven

consumer_families.programs: E_32_4_*, E_2_8_16_4_*, E_16_32_4_2_*, E_8_8_16_2_*, and other ordinary elementwise programs
consumer_families.first_dependent_access: first global load after gidx/lidx/address setup
consumer_families.example: E_32_4_29b...: wait after `int lidx0` and `int alu0`, before `half4 val0 = (*((half4*)(data1_128+alu0)))`
consumer_families.notes: E_2_8_16_4_* kernels with a split producer must resolve which input buffer the edge owns before choosing the insertion point; the generic rule is the first load of that owned buffer

consumer_families.first_dependent_access: first load of the reduced activation inside the Ridx reduce loop
consumer_families.example: r_2_8_4_4_16...: wait after the accumulator is zeroed, before `float val0 = (*(data1_4096+alu4));` in the Ridx loop
consumer_families.notes: the accumulator zeroing and address setup must remain outside the wait so the launched CTA can do useful setup while the producer finishes

consumer_families.first_dependent_access: first x load in the sumsq loop
consumer_families.example: reduce_output_rmsnorm_32_128: wait after `lidx1/lidx2`, `buf0 = 0`, and `alu1`, before `float val0 = (*(data1_4096+(lidx1+alu1+(Ridx2<<3))))`
consumer_families.notes: the weight read occurs later in the epilogue; only the activation x span is the RAW edge, so the wait belongs before the first x load

consumer_families.first_dependent_access: first KV cache load in the staging loop (`kv_load(0,...)` feeding `kstore`)
consumer_families.example: wait after `ksh/vsh/acc/den/mx` setup and before `kstore = ksh[idx].store(kv_load(0, kvh, token_safe, elem_stage), *gate)`
consumer_families.notes: the K and V E_* producers feed the cache span; wait must cover whichever cache span the split edge owns

consumer_families.first_dependent_access: first pout load in the max reduction
consumer_families.example: wait after `head/lane` setup and `max_init`, before `max_update = ... pout[(head * stride + split) * W + M_COL]`
consumer_families.notes: combine reads the score kernel's pout partials; the wait must precede the first pout access

consumer_families.first_dependent_access: first x load in the sumsq reduction
consumer_families.notes: the weight and x spans are both RAW inputs; the x producer is the split edge, the weight is a materialized constant

consumer_families.first_dependent_access: first x load in the `rounded` prelude
consumer_families.example: wait after `group` setup, before the first `x[group*32+i]` load
consumer_families.notes: the provider is a support producer, not a consumer in the Phase A name-pinned set, but is included for completeness of the edge-aware plan

trigger_policies.evidence: Phase C matched grid: native renderer trigger start 394.656/117.472 us shadow/overlap vs end 403.904/99.808 us; QMD pre-exit-at-last-CTA 403.712/99.808 us
trigger_policies.decision_rule: bracket on the real route in Stage 2/4; do not promote a start/end winner from the matched grid alone

trigger_policies.evidence: support output bytes are produced at the body end; a start trigger would expose a producer-data race in the dependent access
trigger_policies.decision_rule: end trigger until a wait-position bracket proves otherwise

open_questions: the renderer must receive per-program split policy from graph metadata rather than process-wide prefixes
multi-producer consumers have no single wait position until the QMD multi-wait/merge question is answered
the wait instruction is SASS `griddepcontrol.wait`; its memory-fence strength and whether it must follow a producer-trigger flush must be verified in Stage 2
wait-placement insertion must be feature-gated so the off path stays byte-identical
